paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. Rahab had heard what the LORD did, and she said of Him, "the LORD your God is God in the heavens above and on the earth below." (Joshua 2:11) She says this while everyone around her is "melting in fear" (Joshua 2:9). Hearing about God is one thing, and deciding it's true is another.

And she didn't keep it up in her head. She asked the spies to show kindness to her family, she agreed to their terms, and she tied the scarlet cord in the window (Joshua 2:12-13, 21). Faith like that has hands. Mine are a mustache, but the principle still stands. I've seen plenty of good intentions, like the dead batteries I shared a junk drawer with that swore they had one more charge in them, and intentions alone don't light up anything.

The passage doesn't hide who Rahab was. It calls her "a prostitute named Rahab" (Joshua 2:1), and yet she's the one who says some of the biggest words about the LORD in the whole chapter. So whoever you are, baker, and whatever your past looks like, what you do with what you've heard about God is what matters here. And friend, this story is NOT done yet.
